(a) Death Gratuity Authorized.—Chapter 81 of title 5, United States Code, is amended by inserting after section 8102 the following:“§ 8102a. Death gratuity for injuries incurred in connection with employee’s service with an Armed Force“(a) Death Gratuity Authorized.—The United States shall pay a death gratuity of up to $100,000 to or for the survivor prescribed by subsection (d) immediately upon receiving official notification of the death of an employee who dies of injuries incurred in connection with the employee’s service with an Armed Force in a contingency operation.“(b) Retroactive Payment in Certain Cases.—At the discretion of the Secretary concerned, subsection (a) may apply in the case of an employee who died, on or after October 7, 2001, and before the date of enactment of this section, as a result of injuries incurred in connection with the employee’s service with an Armed Force in the theater of operations of Operation Enduring Freedom or Operation Iraqi Freedom.“(c) Relationship to Other Benefits.—The death gratuity payable under this section shall be reduced by the amount of any death gratuity provided under section 413 of the Foreign Service Act of 1980, section 1603 of the Emergency Supplemental Appropriations Act for Defense, the Global War on Terror, and Hurricane Recovery, 2006, or any other law of the United States based on the same death.“(d) Eligible Survivors.—
“(1) Subject to paragraph (5), a death gratuity payable upon the death of a person covered by subsection (a) shall be paid to or for the living survivor highest on the following list:“(A) The employee’s surviving spouse.“(B) The employee’s children, as prescribed by paragraph (2), in equal shares.“(C) If designated by the employee, any one or more of the following persons:“(i) The employee’s parents or persons in loco parentis, as prescribed by paragraph (3).“(ii) The employee’s brothers.“(iii) The employee’s sisters.“(D) The employee’s parents or persons in loco parentis, as prescribed by paragraph (3), in equal shares.“(E) The employee’s brothers and sisters in equal shares.
Subparagraphs (C) and (E) of this paragraph include brothers and sisters of the half blood and those through adoption.“(2) Paragraph (1)(B) applies, without regard to age or marital status, to—“(A) legitimate children;“(B) adopted children;“(C) stepchildren who were a part of the decedent’s household at the time of death;“(D) illegitimate children of a female decedent; and“(E) illegitimate children of a male decedent—“(i) who have been acknowledged in writing signed by the decedent;“(ii) who have been judicially determined, before the decedent’s death, to be his children;“(iii) who have been otherwise proved, by evidence satisfactory to the employing agency, to be children of the decedent; or“(iv) to whose support the decedent had been judicially ordered to contribute.“(3) Subparagraphs (C) and (D) of paragraph (1), so far as they apply to parents and persons in loco parentis, include fathers and mothers through adoption, and persons who stood in loco parentis to the decedent for a period of not less than one year at any time before the decedent became an employee. However, only one father and one mother, or their counterparts in loco parentis, may be recognized in any case, and preference shall be given to those who exercised a parental relationship on the date, or most nearly before the date, on which the decedent became an employee.“(4) Beginning on the date of the enactment of this paragraph, a person covered by this section may designate another person to receive not more than 50 percent of the amount payable under this section. The designation shall indicate the percentage of the amount, to be specified only in 10 percent increments up to the maximum of 50 percent, that the designated person may receive. The balance of the amount of the death gratuity shall be paid to or for the living survivors of the person concerned in accordance with subparagraphs (A) through (E) of paragraph (1).“(5) If a person entitled to all or a portion of a death gratuity under paragraph (1) or (4) dies before the person receives the death gratuity, it shall be paid to the living survivor next in the order prescribed by paragraph (1).“(e) Definitions.—(1) The term ‘contingency operation’ has the meaning given to that term in section 1482a(c) of title 10, United States Code.“(2) The term ‘employee’ has the meaning provided in section 8101 of this title, but also includes a nonappropriated fund instrumentality employee, as defined in section 1587(a)(1) of title 10.”. 
    (b) Clerical Amendment.—The table of sections at the beginning of chapter 81 of such title is amended by inserting after the item relating to section 8102 the following:

“8102a. 
Death gratuity for injuries incurred in connection with employee’s service with an Armed Force.”.

fable.w: This section creates a death gratuity benefit for survivors of federal employees who die of injuries incurred in a contingency operation, and sets the order of eligible survivors. The tempting reading is that an employee's designation of a beneficiary, or proof of parentage by "evidence satisfactory to the employing agency", is outside involvement in a federal decision. Those are benefit-eligibility mechanics, not consultation, comment, hearing, advisory-body, or right-to-sue provisions. No outside party is brought into a federal policy decision.
fable.s: The United States shall pay a death gratuity of up to $100,000 to or for the survivor prescribed by subsection (d)

qwen_block.w: This section establishes a benefit program (death gratuity) for survivors of federal employees. It defines eligibility and payment procedures but does not require consultation, coordination, or participation from outside parties in the decision-making process. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and this text describes the automatic payment of a benefit rather than a participatory process.
qwen_block.s: The United States shall pay a death gratuity of up to $100,000 to or for the survivor prescribed by subsection (d) immediately upon receiving official notification of the death of an employee who dies of injuries incurred in connection with the employee’s service with an Armed Force in a contingency operation.

opus.w: The section creates a death-gratuity benefit and sets out who among the survivors gets it, in order of priority. Naming a beneficiary or giving the employing agency evidence of a family relationship is part of claiming a benefit, which the definition excludes. Nothing here requires rulemaking, consultation with outside entities, hearings, advisory bodies, or a right to sue over a federal decision.
opus.s: The United States shall pay a death gratuity of up to $100,000 to or for the survivor prescribed by subsection (d) immediately upon receiving official notification of the death of an employee
opus.b:
I'm labelling this section **No**: it sets up a death-gratuity benefit and contains no outside-party process in any federal decision.

1. **Tempting reading:** Two parts of the section involve people outside the government. Employees can name who receives the gratuity, and survivors can prove a child relationship "by evidence satisfactory to the employing agency." That could look like outsiders taking part in a federal decision.
2. **Why it fails:** Both are part of claiming or directing an individual benefit, and the definition excludes applications for benefits. The section also has no rulemaking authority, comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes a death gratuity benefit for survivors of employees who die in service. It defines eligibility, payment amounts, and the order of survivors. The definition of participation explicitly excludes 'applications for benefits or grants.' Designating a beneficiary is part of the benefit administration, not a consultation with the government on a decision. There is no requirement for the government to consult with outside parties before making a decision; the decision is triggered by the event of death and governed by statutory criteria.
qwen_chat.s: The United States shall pay a death gratuity of up to $100,000 to or for the survivor prescribed by subsection (d) immediately upon receiving official notification of the death of an employee who dies of injuries incurred in connection with the employee’s service with an Armed Force in a contingency operation.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the ability of an employee to designate a beneficiary (subsection (d)(4)) constitutes "participation" because it involves an outside party influencing the distribution of funds. However, the definition explicitly states: "It does not include applications for benefits or grants." Designating a beneficiary for a death gratuity is part of the administrative process for receiving a benefit, not a consultation or coordination with the government regarding a federal policy decision. The section is purely about the eligibility and payment of a benefit to survivors.
